sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 10.9A. In Canvas 1, adjust Domain Randomization spread sigma DR between 0.1 and 2.0 to observe trajectory support expansion. In Canvas 2, adjust LiDAR beam counts and obstacle distance to witness Beer-Lambert atmospheric attenuation and pulse dropouts.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: In Simulator 10.9A, test setting DR spread to 0.8. Look how the randomized trajectory envelope brackets the physical ground truth target! Then push obstacle distance to 40 meters to observe optical LiDAR attenuation in dense fog.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: A 905-nanometer LiDAR emits 100 Watts in dense fog with extinction coefficient 0.02 per meter. For an obstacle with diffuse reflectivity 0.40, calculate returned intensity at 10 meters and 50 meters, and verify detectability against the 0.005 Watt per square meter threshold.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: For Checkpoint 1, calculate the radiometric LiDAR power: at 10 meters, returned intensity is 0.2681 Watts per square meter. But at 50 meters, quadratic drop-off and atmospheric decay reduce power to 0.002165 Watts per square meter. Is the obstacle detectable?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Brilliant optical derivation! At 10 meters, returned power is 0.2681 Watts per square meter, easily exceeding the 0.005 threshold. At 50 meters, the quadratic distance term 2500 combined with exponential extinction factor 0.1353 yields 0.002165 Watts per square meter. Because 0.002165 is less than 0.005, the pulse is undetectable, causing point cloud dropout!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Review your radiometric calculations. The returned optical intensity at 50 meters is 40 divided by 2500 times exp of minus 2.0, which equals 0.016 times 0.1353, or 0.002165 Watts per square meter. Since 0.002165 is below the 0.005 threshold, the sensor fails to register the obstacle.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Interactive Lab 10.9B. In Canvas 3, monitor the Maximum Mean Discrepancy projection in RKHS feature space. In Canvas 4, click 'Simulate 5,000 Virtual Miles' to accumulate autonomous mileage and verify whether MMD falls below our certified 0.20 transfer threshold.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: In Simulator 10.9B, click 'Simulate 5,000 Virtual Miles'! Watch virtual mileage accumulate and MMD settle to 0.185, activating the green 'Transfer: Ready' status with an estimated 94.2% zero-shot transfer rate.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: Given synthetic velocity errors {1.0, 3.0} and physical velocity errors {2.0, 4.0} with Gaussian RBF kernel exp(-0.5 * (x - y)^2), calculate Mean K xx, Mean K yy, Mean K xy, and derive the empirical MMD squared and MMD score.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: For Checkpoint 2, calculate the pairwise RBF kernel matrices: K xx and K yy have mean 0.5677, while cross-matrix K xy has mean 0.4577. Compute MMD squared as Mean K xx minus 2 Mean K xy plus Mean K yy!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Exact RKHS kernel calculation! Mean K xx is 0.5677, Mean K yy is 0.5677, and Mean K xy is 0.4577. MMD squared is 0.5677 minus 2 times 0.4577 plus 0.5677, which equals 0.2200. Taking the square root gives an empirical MMD of approximately 0.4690!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Check your arithmetic: Mean K xx and Mean K yy are both (1 + 0.1353 + 0.1353 + 1)/4 = 0.5677. Mean K xy is (3 * 0.6065 + 0.0111)/4 = 0.4577. MMD squared is 1.1353 minus 0.9154 = 0.2200, yielding MMD ≈ 0.4690.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3: Which end-to-end cyber-physical architecture guarantees robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer and safety compliance for a commercial autonomous delivery robot fleet in complex urban environments?

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: For Checkpoint 3, evaluate the complete validation pipeline: GPU-accelerated multi-body physics, radiometric LiDAR and sensor degradation, domain randomization satisfying support coverage, adversarial corner-case fuzzing, and MMD reality gating!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Mastery confirmed! A certified autonomous validation pipeline combines GPU multi-body physics, radiometric sensor ray-casting with atmospheric extinction, domain randomization covering the physical parameter support, adversarial corner-case fuzzing, and MMD reality gating prior to physical deployment!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Notice the failure modes: naive geometric ray-casters fail in bad weather, and training without domain randomization causes reality gap collapse. A production pipeline requires physics-based sensor degradation, domain randomization, adversarial fuzzing, and MMD reality gating.
